outcomes: A team turns a repository its monorepo tool already describes into a Putnami workspace with one command
After a change to one package of an adopted Pants repository, putnami test runs that package and its dependents through Pants, and Putnami's cache stores nothing
After a change to one package of an adopted Bazel workspace, putnami test runs that package and its dependents through Bazel, and Putnami's cache stores nothing
A team adopts a Nx repository in the mode it picks: import, where Putnami's runner and cache take over, or delegate, where Nx and its cache keep running each target

After a change to one project of a moon repository adopted in delegate mode, putnami test runs moon on that project and its dependents, and Putnami's cache stores nothing; adopted in import mode, its projects run the Putnami extension of their language
After a change to one package of a Turborepo repository adopted in delegate mode, putnami test runs turbo on that package and its dependents, and Putnami's cache stores nothing
After a change to one project of a Rush repository adopted in delegate mode, putnami build runs rush build on that project and its dependents, and Putnami's cache stores nothing
nonGoals: Reading a monorepo tool's configuration in the CLI: the tool's stack extension owns it
Choosing between import and delegate for the team: the mode is asked, given with --mode, or import without a terminal

text: putnami init --from pants, at the root of a repository that holds pants.toml, writes a workspace that declares @putnami/pants, installs it, and runs putnami projects sync, which writes each package's putnami.json through the extension's sync task and names by path two directories that share a name.

Without pants.toml it fails with a usage error that names the file, and an unknown --from value fails with a usage error that lists the supported tools. --from does not combine with --project or --extension.

On the Pants fixture of the putnami observe detector, with @putnami/pants and pants on PATH, projects sync writes each package's edges. putnami test --impacted runs pants test at the workspace root on each changed package and each package that depends on it, never on one it depends on;
a requirements or lockfile change, wherever the file lies, runs the packages that use it.
It reads their reports and neither looks up nor stores a Putnami cache entry.

putnami init --from bazel, at the root of a repository that holds MODULE.bazel, WORKSPACE or WORKSPACE.bazel, writes a workspace that declares @putnami/bazel, installs it, and runs putnami projects sync, which writes each package's putnami.json through the extension's sync task.
Without one of those files it fails with a usage error that names them.

On the Bazel fixture of the putnami observe detector, with @putnami/bazel and bazel on PATH, projects sync writes each package's edges. putnami test --impacted runs bazel coverage at the workspace root on each changed package and each package that depends on it, never on one it depends on;
a MODULE.bazel change runs every package.
It reads their reports and neither looks up nor stores a Putnami cache entry.

putnami init --from nx, at the root of a repository that holds nx.json, writes a workspace that declares @putnami/nx, records the mode in its options, also declares @putnami/typescript in import mode, installs them and runs putnami projects sync, which writes each Nx project's putnami.json through the extension's sync task.
Without nx.json it fails with a usage error that names the file.

For a tool that offers both modes, putnami init --from <tool> asks import or delegate in a terminal, with import preselected, and imports without a terminal. --mode import|delegate skips the question;
a value the tool does not offer, Pants offering delegate alone, fails with a usage error that lists its modes, and --mode without --from is a usage error.

Rerun in a workspace that already exists, putnami init --from <tool> runs the workspace sync tasks as a dry run with the mode it resolves and the extensions --apply would declare, which each reads as declared, so it prints what --apply would change and the mode change, and writes nothing.
With --apply it records the mode and runs putnami projects sync.

requirements.text: Rerun with --mode delegate in a workspace that imported, with no import list, putnami init --from <tool> names in its preview each extension the import declared, @putnami/typescript or the language extensions moon's sync declares, and with --apply removes from the workspace config, the lock and the disk each one no putnami.json names after the sync, keeping with a note each one a project still names (D-070).

On the Nx fixture of the putnami observe detector, after putnami init --from nx --mode delegate --apply with a stub nx on PATH, putnami test after a change to one project runs nx run <project>:test at the workspace root on that project and each project that depends on it, never on one it depends on, stores no Putnami cache entry and records delegatedTo nx.

text: putnami init --from moon, at the root of a repository that holds .moon/workspace.yml, writes a workspace that declares @putnami/moon, records the mode in its options, installs it and runs putnami projects sync, which writes each moon project's putnami.json, then installs the language extensions the sync declared.
Without .moon/workspace.yml it fails with a usage error naming the file.

requirements.text: On the moon fixture of the putnami observe detector, putnami init --from moon --mode import --apply writes the project graph observe reads, moves to its language's extension each moon task that extension runs with the same tool, keeps every other task and each project of a language without an extension on @putnami/moon, lists each task it keeps in its output, and putnami lint,test,build then pass.

On the moon fixture of the putnami observe detector, with moon on PATH, putnami init --from moon --mode delegate --apply then putnami test --impacted after a change to one project runs moon run <project>:<task> at the workspace root on that project and each project that depends on it, never on one it depends on, records delegatedTo moon, and neither looks up nor stores a Putnami cache entry.

text: putnami init --from turbo, at the root of a repository that holds turbo.json, writes a workspace that declares @putnami/turbo, and @putnami/typescript in import mode, records the mode in options["@putnami/turbo"].mode, installs the extensions, and runs putnami projects sync.
Without turbo.json it fails with a usage error that names the file.

On the Turborepo fixture of the putnami observe detector, after putnami init --from turbo --mode delegate --apply, a change to one package makes putnami test run turbo run test on that package and on each package that depends on it, never on one it depends on;
it stores no Putnami cache entry and records delegatedTo turbo.

requirements.text: On the same fixture, in import mode, the sync keeps the edges putnami observe reads, gives a TypeScript package @putnami/typescript for a task whose script already runs bun test and disables @putnami/turbo for it, and lists each tsc or vitest task it leaves on Turborepo.

With a monorepo tool's extension declared, putnami init --from <tool> and putnami projects sync make a project only of a directory the tool lists or that holds its own putnami.json: a workspace member for Turborepo, a project of rush.json, moon or the Nx graph, a Bazel package outside .bazelignore and REPO.bazel ignore_directories, a Pants BUILD directory. The sync counts the directories it left out. When the tool cannot list them, it warns, keeps only putnami.json directories and does not prune.

text: putnami init --from nx|turbo --import <path>,<path> in delegate mode adds each path not listed yet to options["@putnami/<tool>"].import and declares @putnami/typescript.
In a workspace that exists, it previews the change and the sync's dry run with that list, and writes only with --apply, which records it, installs the extensions and runs projects sync.
A new workspace records it with the mode. --import with another tool, no path, or import mode is a usage error.

requirements.text: On the delegated Nx and Turborepo fixtures of the putnami observe detector, with pricing's scripts running bun build and bun test, putnami init --from <tool> --import /packages/pricing --apply then putnami lint,test,build pass: pricing runs on @putnami/typescript with Putnami's cache, and api still runs through the tool, its results recording delegatedTo <tool>.

text: putnami init --from rush, at the root of a repository that holds rush.json, declares @putnami/rush, records the mode in its options, also declares @putnami/typescript in import mode, installs them and runs projects sync, whose Rush sync task writes each Rush project's putnami.json.
In import mode the TypeScript install writes the root package.json with the projects as workspaces.
Without rush.json it is a usage error that names the file.

On the Rush fixture of the putnami observe detector, an import writes each Rush project as a TypeScript project whose dependencies are the edges putnami observe reads, keeps a script whose tool @putnami/typescript does not run on rushx and lists it, then putnami lint,test,build passes and no task runs rush.
A command-line.json bulk command whose name is not build, test or lint appears as unmapped, and validate fails with rush.sync_stale once a script changes.
On the Rush fixture of the putnami observe detector, with @putnami/rush and rush on PATH, putnami init --from rush --mode delegate --apply writes each project's edges.

After a change to one project, putnami build --impacted runs rush build --to <package> at the workspace root on that project and each project that depends on it, never on one it depends on, records delegatedTo rush, and neither looks up nor stores a Putnami cache entry.
